verdicts.summary: Tried: independence 1 Jan 1960, the 1 Oct 1961 union with Southern Cameroons (plebiscite 11 Feb 1961), the 1972 and 1984 renames, the 2006 and 2008 Bakassi handovers: all on the pages with the years. The 1960/1961 area difference (41,368 km2) matches Southern Cameroons (Nord-Ouest + Sud-Ouest). Verified in the Cliopatria geometry that the 1961-2023 shape holds Bakassi (points 8.62E 4.75N and 8.67E 4.67N inside), so the adjust and the 2008 keyframe are right. Could not break it. The Bakassi mirror is missing on the Nigeria side (cross_checks).
One event (independence 27 April 1960) confirmed; the page records no border change after 1960; area 56,508 against 56,785 km2. Nothing to break within the 1-2 page budget.

All ten independence losses are confirmed on the Decolonisation of Africa tables with their dates, and reading the row as the remainder of British Africa is sound. But the keyframe corrections rest on a false premise: the 1961 Cliopatria polygon is not 'cell for cell' the nine territories. Read from the Cliopatria geometry (features cache), it also holds Zanzibar, Pemba, Mafia Island, Socotra and the Seychelles. So the 1962-1965 minus-corrections keep Zanzibar and Pemba after the Sultanate's independence of 10 Dec 1963 (drawn twice with sultanate-of-zanzibar), and the 1966 intersect drops the Seychelles and Socotra with no event. The 1968 'gain' of the Seychelles from british-colonial-empire is spurious: the islands were in this shape from 1961. Back to the author.
